findings.evidence: Fields at lines 88-98; the derivations above use only `same_iff` and `over_partner`. `Function.Involutive.toPerm` exists: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Fin/Rev.lean:36.
findings.fix: Keep only `same_iff` and `over_partner` as fields and restate the other three as lemmas (`partner_ne`, `partner_partner` already exists as a `simp` lemma, `visit_surjective` via `Fintype.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise`). Since involutivity is then forced, `partner` can also be a plain `Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n)` with the permutation recovered by `Function.Involutive.toPerm`, removing the `Equiv.swap`/inverse boilerplate at construction sites (line 216).
findings.issue: Three of the six axioms are redundant. `partner_ne` (line 92) follows from `over_partner` (line 98): if `partner i = i` then `over i = !over i`. `partner_involutive` (line 90) follows from `same_iff` + `partner_ne`: `visit (partner (partner i)) = visit (partner i) = visit i`, so `same_iff` gives `partner (partner i) = i ∨ partner (partner i) = partner i`, and the second case makes `partner i` a fixed point. `visit_surjective` (line 96) follows by counting: `same_iff` makes each nonempty fibre of `visit` exactly `{i, partner i}` of card 2, and `2 * n / 2 = n = Fintype.card (Fin n)` forces every fibre nonempty. Every construction (`empty`, `oneCrossingPositive`, and every future PD/diagram conversion) must discharge all three.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/Perm/Sign.lean:357 `def sign [Fintype α] : Perm α →* ℤˣ`; TauCeti already uses `ℤˣ`/`SignType` elsewhere (code/TauCeti/KnotTheory/Grid/EulerCharacteristic.lean, Grid/Grading/Parity.lean).
findings.fix: Use `sign : Fin n → ℤˣ`; then `writhe D = ∑ c, ((D.sign c : ℤ))`, `mirror` is `fun c => -D.sign c`, and `writhe_mirror` follows from `Units.val_neg` and `Finset.sum_neg_distrib` without the bespoke `neg`/`toInt` API.
findings.issue: `CrossingSign` plus `neg`, `neg_neg`, `toInt`, `toInt_neg` (lines 40-69) duplicates Mathlib's ±1 sign group `ℤˣ`, which is the convention Mathlib uses for exactly this data (`Equiv.Perm.sign : Perm α →* ℤˣ`). The hand-rolled type has no monoid structure, so downstream sign arithmetic (writhe additivity, skein/Reidemeister sign bookkeeping) must reprove group facts instead of reusing `neg_neg`, `Units.val_neg`, and `Finset.sum` lemmas.

summary: The `OrientedGaussCode` structure carries three redundant proof fields (`partner_involutive`, `partner_ne`, `visit_surjective`), all derivable from `same_iff` + `over_partner`, so every present and future constructor pays for them; and `CrossingSign` re-implements the ±1 sign group that Mathlib already provides as `ℤˣ`.
